Half of Control Resonant's players were 'new' to the franchise
Players unfamiliar with Remedy's 'new weird' action series helped drive Control Resonant to over one million units sold in just three weeks.
Bryant Francis
,
Senior Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 3, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
via Remedy Entertainment
Remedy Entertainment has a particularly strong bit of good news standing out in its
third-quarter financial results
for fiscal year 2026. It's already riding a successful quarter thanks to the release of
Control Resonant
, raking in €39.6 million (about $44.3 million) in revenue, with an EBITDA of €6.8 million and operating profit of €0.6 million. That marks a 226 percent increase in its revenue, up from about €12.2 million from the same quarter in 2025.
That'd be a positive result for any developer, but for a cult-hit producer like Remedy that builds its business on a loyal fanbase, it has even better news to share: about half of
Control Resonant
's purchases to date have been made by players who didn't play the first game,
Control
.
"Reaching new players was a key goal for this game, and these early result indicates a growing audience for the franchise and for Remedy," said CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon in a statement to investors, noting that
Resonant
is the first self-published game from the studio.
Related:
Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang pushes back on characterizations of her departure
Many developers have reported that the task of finding new audiences in 2026 is proving to be a tall challenge, as data indicates many players sticking with their
existing favorite games
instead of trying out new ones.
Another interesting data point concerning audience demographics: console players in Brazil are becoming a bigger market for Remedy's games. That reflects what we saw
at Gamescom LATAM
earlier this year, where
Control Resonant
creative director Mikael Kasurinen made time for a meet-and-greet with an enthusiastic crowd of players. According to Gaudechon, this trend reflects the traction the company saw in "growth markets" since its pre-order campaign began.
It's not totally clear yet how this batch of new players will boost Remedy's back catalogue of games. Remedy stated that sales of the original
Control
"exceeded both the comparison period and the first two quarters of this year," but provided no additional numbers.
Looking ahead, Remedy is looking to capitalize on
Control Resonant
's outstanding 2.4 million wishlists. "Our priority now is to get CONTROL Resonant into the hands of more players. Excellent player reviews, penetration in all our target markets and a substantial outstanding wishlist base give a solid foundation for the game’s longer-term sales potential, supported by both organic visibility as well as our targeted marketing activities."
"As with the launch, we will invest with discipline, prioritizing actions with a clear return."
